card.name: Hedged claims in science news
card.fires_on: Words like "could", "deadly", "study" and "tied" in science-news headlines and lead sentences. They come just before a finding or a possible benefit or risk is stated.

modes.label: Hedging verb
modes.description: "could" or "tied" introducing a possible result or link in a news claim.
modes.example: Better use of technology<< could>> be the key to improving public schools,

modes.label: "deadly" before a disease term
modes.description: The adjective "deadly" placed before a virus, bacteria or protein in research reports.
modes.example: researchers at the University of Pittsburgh have discovered a potential treatment for<< deadly>>, drug-resistant bacterial infections

modes.label: New study headline
modes.description: "study" after "a new" at the start of a health news item.
modes.example: A new<< study>> suggests obese girls may be at increased risk

card.writes: The promoted tokens are mostly odd word-pieces, so there is no clear effect beyond a weak push toward word-starts.
card.plain: It lights up on the cautious or dramatic wording in science news, like "could" or "deadly", just before the finding is stated.
